businessProblem: Yes Bank faces deteriorating asset quality, failed capital-raising attempts, fragile depositor confidence, and known governance and risk-management concerns as of 4 March 2020. Systemic implications make this a financial stability issue. Diagnose root causes and recommend highest-priority action plan before regulatory intervention.

evidence.finding: Yes Bank's asset quality is deteriorating with high stressed and non-performing asset exposure
evidence.source: Yes Bank Q3 FY2019-20 statutory release, regulatory disclosures

evidence.finding: Bank needs capital and has failed to secure sufficient credible capital through private-market attempts
evidence.source: Public reporting, Yale financial crises case material

evidence.finding: Capital adequacy insufficient to absorb stressed asset losses without external injection
Depositor and market confidence under pressure — franchise value at risk if confidence collapses
Yes Bank's size and interconnectedness means failure carries systemic implications for Indian financial system
evidence.source: Yale financial crises case material, public reporting

evidence.finding: Known governance and risk-management concerns contributed to the asset-quality deterioration
RBI actively monitoring capital adequacy and asset quality — regulatory intervention increasingly probable
Private capital-raising window closing — market confidence in management's ability to execute capital plan is low

ownerConstraintProfile.followThroughRisk: CRITICAL — window for self-rescue has effectively closed
ownerConstraintProfile.resistanceToChange: HIGH — management had resisted adequate governance reform
ownerConstraintProfile.managementCapability: CRITICALLY COMPROMISED — failed multiple capital-raising attempts
ownerConstraintProfile.keyPersonDependency: HIGH — prior management's decisions created current crisis
ownerConstraintProfile.accountabilityWeakness: CRITICAL — governance failures allowed asset-quality problem to develop
